# ZSWatch Companion App — Copilot Instructions

## Project Overview

Monorepo for the **ZSWatch** smartwatch companion app (Flutter) and reference materials. The Flutter app (`zswatch_app/`) communicates with ZSWatch firmware over BLE using the Gadgetbridge/BangleJS JSON protocol. The firmware (`ZSWatch-Firmware/`) is a Zephyr RTOS application; the Gadgetbridge fork (`Gadgetbridge/`) is protocol reference only (not a runtime dependency).

## Architecture

### Directory Layout (`zswatch_app/lib/`)

| Layer | Path | Responsibility |
|-------|------|----------------|
| **Entry** | `main.dart`, `app.dart` | Bootstrap, provider init, theme |
| **UI** | `ui/screens/`, `ui/widgets/`, `ui/navigation/` | Screens per feature, `go_router` navigation |
| **Providers** | `providers/` | Riverpod providers — one file per domain (e.g. `health_providers.dart`) |
| **Services** | `services/` | Business logic: BLE, protocol, DFU, health sync, notification/media bridges |
| **Data** | `data/database/`, `data/models/`, `data/repositories/` | Drift (SQLite) DB, domain models, repository pattern |
| **Core** | `core/constants/`, `core/extensions/`, `core/theme/` | BLE UUIDs, utilities, dark theme |

### Key Architectural Decisions

- **State management**: Riverpod (`flutter_riverpod`). Providers are in `providers/` and wire services → UI. Use `Provider`, `StreamProvider`, `StateNotifierProvider` patterns already in use — do NOT introduce `ChangeNotifier` or `Bloc`.
- **Database**: Drift with code generation. Tables in `data/database/tables/`. After schema changes, run `dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` to regenerate `app_database.g.dart`.
- **BLE protocol**: JSON-over-NUS (Nordic UART Service). Outgoing: `GB({json})\n`. Incoming: raw JSON. Protocol implemented in `services/protocol/gadgetbridge_protocol.dart`, message types in `message_types.dart`. Refer to `gadgetbridge_api.txt` for the complete message format spec.
- **Protocol routing principle**: Use Gadgetbridge protocol for everything it supports (notifications, music, weather, GPS, activity). Use standard GATT services where they exist (Heart Rate 0x180D, sensors). Only use Extended API for features Gadgetbridge doesn't cover.
- **Platform bridges**: Android notification forwarding and media control use native Kotlin via `MethodChannel`/`EventChannel` — iOS uses ANCS/AMS natively on the watch (app is no-op).

### Data Flow (BLE Communication)

```
Phone App                                    ZSWatch Firmware
─────────                                    ────────────────
WatchService ←→ GadgetbridgeProtocol ←→ GattOperations ←→ NUS (BLE) ←→ ble_gadgetbridge.c
     ↕                                                        ↕
Providers (Riverpod)                              Zephyr BLE stack
     ↕
UI Screens
```

`WatchService` (`services/watch_service.dart`) is the central hub: manages connection lifecycle, routes protocol messages, exposes streams consumed by providers.

## Build & Development

```bash
cd zswatch_app
flutter pub get
dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs  # generate Drift DB, Riverpod
flutter run                                                # debug on connected device
```

DFU plugin uses a Git dependency fork: `Flutter-nRF-Connect-Device-Manager/` (MCUmgr/SMP protocol for firmware updates).

### Linting

Strict mode enabled (`strict-casts`, `strict-inference`, `strict-raw-types`). Enforced rules include `cancel_subscriptions`, `close_sinks`, `unawaited_futures`, `prefer_single_quotes`, `prefer_const_constructors`. Generated files (`*.g.dart`) are excluded.

## Conventions & Patterns

- **Provider files**: One per domain in `providers/`. Each provider file exports relevant services/state. Initialize services by reading providers in `app.dart._initializeBle()`.
- **Service pattern**: Services are plain Dart classes holding `BehaviorSubject`/`StreamController` streams. Providers create and expose them. See `WatchService`, `HealthSyncService`, `DfuService`.
- **Repository pattern**: Repositories in `data/repositories/` wrap Drift queries. Each repository takes `AppDatabase` in its constructor.
- **Models**: Domain models in `data/models/` — use `copyWith`, `Equatable` where applicable. DB entities are generated by Drift.
- **Screens**: Feature screens in `ui/screens/<feature>/`. Use `ConsumerWidget`/`ConsumerStatefulWidget` for Riverpod access.
- **Routes**: Defined as constants in `AppRoutes` (abstract final class) in `ui/navigation/app_router.dart`.
- **BLE UUIDs**: All UUIDs in `core/constants/ble_constants.dart` as `abstract final class` groupings (e.g. `NusUuids`, `HeartRateUuids`, `SensorServiceUuids`).
- **Logging**: Use `debugPrint('[ClassName] message')` with class name prefix — NOT `print()`.

## DFU (Device Firmware Update) System

DFU is the most complex subsystem, spanning three services, two upload protocols, and a multi-step extraction pipeline.

### Service Architecture (`services/dfu/`)

| File | Class | Responsibility |
|------|-------|----------------|
| `firmware_manager.dart` | `FirmwareManager` | Downloads from GitHub (releases + CI), extracts zip archives, parses `manifest.json` |
| `dfu_service.dart` | `DfuService` | Wraps `mcumgr_flutter` for MCUmgr/SMP image upload with progress tracking |
| `filesystem_upload_service.dart` | `FilesystemUploadService` | Uploads filesystem images (e.g. LVGL resources) via MCUmgr `FsManager` |

### Firmware Acquisition Pipeline

```
GitHub Release asset (e.g. watchdk@1_nrf5340_cpuapp_debug.zip)
  │
  ├─ FirmwareManager.downloadReleaseAsset()
  │   └─ Downloads zip, calls _extractReleaseArchive()
  │
  └─ _extractReleaseArchive()
      ├─ Extracts dfu_application.zip → FirmwareImage
      └─ Extracts lvgl_resources_raw.bin → FilesystemImage (optional)
          └─ Returns ReleaseExtractionResult { firmwareImage, filesystemImage? }

dfu_application.zip
  │
  └─ FirmwareManager.extractZip()
      ├─ Parses manifest.json → Map<filename, ManifestEntry>
      │   ManifestEntry { file, imageIndex, version, board }
      │   imageIndex: 0=app internal, 1=netCore, 2=app external
      └─ Extracts .bin files → List<FirmwareImage> sorted by slot
```

### Upload Flows

**Firmware update** (`DfuService.startUpdate()`):
1. Creates `DeviceUpdateManager` from `mcumgr_flutter`
2. Reads `.bin` files into `Image(image: slot, data: bytes)` list
3. Uploads via MCUmgr with `FirmwareUpgradeMode.confirmOnly` (confirms image after upload so device boots new firmware)
4. State machine: `preparing → uploading → validating → applying → rebooting → completed`
5. Critical phases (`uploading`, `validating`, `applying`) should not be interrupted

**Filesystem update** (`FilesystemUploadService.startUpload()`):
1. Creates `FsManager` from `mcumgr_flutter`
2. Reads `lvgl_resources_raw.bin` bytes
3. Uploads to device path (e.g. `/lfs1/lvgl_resources`) via MCUmgr filesystem commands
4. State machine: `idle → uploading → completed/failed`

**Combined "Start Both"**: Filesystem upload completes first, then firmware images upload (order matters — firmware reboot would interrupt filesystem upload).

### Key Implementation Details

- `FirmwareImage.slot` maps to MCUmgr `image_index` from `manifest.json` — determines which flash slot receives the image
- `FilesystemImage.targetPath` comes from `FilesystemConstants` — the on-device path for LVGL resources
- `ReleaseExtractionResult` bundles both image types from a single release download
- `DfuState` uses `BehaviorSubject` with `copyWith` pattern — speed calculation runs on a 1-second timer separate from progress updates
- `DeviceUpdateManager.getInstance()` can fail if a previous manager wasn't cleaned up — the service handles this with kill-and-retry logic
- Local `.bin` or `.zip` files can also be loaded via `FirmwareManager.loadLocalFile()` + `extractZip()`, bypassing GitHub entirely

### Provider Wiring (`providers/dfu_providers.dart`, `providers/filesystem_providers.dart`)

Providers expose `DfuService`, `FirmwareManager`, and `FilesystemUploadService` as singletons. The firmware update screen reads state via `dfuStateProvider`/`dfuStatusProvider` and triggers actions through the service providers directly.

## AI Testbench (`ai_testbench/`)

Standalone Flutter desktop app for benchmarking and evaluating on-device LLM models before shipping them in the companion app. It tests the same prompts and schemas used in production (`chrono_ai_flow` package) against local GGUF models via `fllama`.

### What It Tests

| Benchmark | Service | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| **Structured extraction** | `model_benchmark_service.dart` | Validates LLM outputs valid JSON matching `chrono_ai_flow` schema (intent, title, datetime fields) |
| **Time extraction** | `time_extraction_benchmark_service.dart` | End-to-end: transcript → LLM extraction → `chrono_dart` parsing → resolved `DateTime` |
| **Correction** | `correction_benchmark_service.dart` | Verifies LLM can fix common STT errors (homophones, filler, punctuation) |

### Running Benchmarks

```bash
cd ai_testbench
flutter pub get

# Interactive GUI
flutter run -d linux

# Headless (compiled for consistent timing)
flutter build linux --release
./build/linux/x64/release/bundle/ai_testbench --headless --output results.json
./build/linux/x64/release/bundle/ai_testbench --headless-time --model Qwen3.5-2B-Q4_K_M.gguf
./build/linux/x64/release/bundle/ai_testbench --headless-correction --model-dir models/
```

### Key Files

- `lib/main.dart` — Entry point with headless mode dispatch (`--headless`, `--headless-time`, `--headless-correction`)
- `lib/services/llm_service.dart` — `fllama` wrapper (`LlmService`) for inference with configurable parameters
- `lib/prompts/` — Prompt templates (delegates to `chrono_ai_flow` for production prompts)
- `benchmark_results/` — Saved benchmark summaries (Markdown)

### Dependencies

- **fllama** — Flutter llama.cpp bindings for on-device inference
- **chrono_ai_flow** — Shared prompt templates and JSON schema (local package at `../packages/chrono_ai_flow`)
- **chrono_dart** — Natural language time expression parsing

### Notes

- GGUF model files go in `models/` (gitignored — download separately from HuggingFace)
- Native `.so` libraries go in `native_libs/` (gitignored — build from llama.cpp if using the CLI `bin/` runner)
- Test cases are defined inline in the service files — add new cases there
- The testbench shares the same `chrono_ai_flow` package as the main app, so prompt changes are tested against both
